summary.title: Achieving Gold-Medal-Level Olympiad Reasoning via Simple and Unified Scaling

details: Olympiad problems require rigorous, complete proofs, but strong compact reasoning backbones optimize for final answers and lack disciplined proof-search/self-checking behavior; frontier gold-medal systems rely on very large models or heavy specialized search.
Question: can a single compact, domain-unified recipe push a modest post-trained backbone to olympiad gold level across math and physics?

A unified three-part recipe (yielding the model SU-01): (1) long-CoT SFT on solution/self-verification/self-refinement traces presented in descending-perplexity (reverse-perplexity) order so each epoch starts with the trajectories most mismatched to the current policy and consolidates on familiar ones; (2) two-stage RL that first scales behavior with binary verifiable outcome rewards (GSPO), then switches the target to proof quality using a generative proof-level reward model plus self-refinement prompts built from failed rollouts and replay of rare successful hard-problem trajectories; (3) test-time scaling via an iterative solve–verify–refine loop with structured bug reports and accept/reject verdicts.
Framing: 'specializable generalist' — specialize a broadly capable post-trained model toward rigorous proof reasoning while preserving scientific breadth.
Initialization from the post-trained P1-30B-A3B (MoE) reasoning model rather than a base model.

SFT prompts from olympiad/math sources (Evan Chen materials, AoPS, Shuzhimi Forum, competition books, DeepMath difficulty>=6), NaturalReasoning STEM, Nemotron chat/IF, and coding (Eurus-2-RL, OpenCodeReasoning-2); trajectories distilled from DeepSeek-V3.2-Speciale, decontaminated, and capped at 8,192 tokens → 338K examples including self-verify and self-refine traces.
4 epochs, batch size 128, Adam lr 1e-5 with cosine decay, shuffling disabled to preserve the descending-PPL curriculum; validation truncation rate below 5% used as adaptation criterion.
Separate RL pool after dedup/decontamination and rejection sampling: 8,967 verifiable + 16,287 non-verifiable (proof) prompts, including OPC proof corpus and P1 physics data.

GSPO objective with unnormalized group-relative advantage, 200 total steps (96 coarse + 104 refined), prompt batch 128, 8 rollouts/prompt, up to 160K-token responses, KL and entropy coefficients 0, frozen MoE router; 64 GPUs with slime + SGLang.

Coarse reward: layered verifier (canonical matching → Math-Verify → gpt-oss-120b generative check). Refined reward: DeepSeekMath-V2 binary proof reward (except physics) with anti-hack preprocessing; self-refinement ratio 0.2 triggered when group reward < 0.5; ExGRPO-style replay at ratio 0.25, admit when only one rollout succeeds, retire at >=4 successes, lowest-entropy stored trajectory selected.

Model-agnostic solve → refine → verify (structured bug report) → verdict loop following Huang et al.; up to 30 exploration cycles per run, accept after 5 consecutive passes, abort after 10 consecutive failures, up to 10 independent runs per problem.
Generation at temperature 1.0, top-p 0.95, up to 160K tokens (131K–256K depending on benchmark).

Answer-verifiable: IMO-AnswerBench, AMO-Bench, AIME 2025/2026, FrontierScience-Olympiad. Proof-oriented: IMO-ProofBench (graded 0/1/6/7 by Gemini-2.5-Pro per official protocol), FrontierScience-Research (GPT-5-high judge).
Official competitions: IMO 2025, USAMO 2026 (three IMO/CMO gold-medal experts score independently; worst of three reported), IPhO 2024/2025 with P1-style physics grading.

Similar-size baselines: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, Nemotron-Cascade-2-30B-A3B, GLM-4.7-Flash, Gemma-4-31B, plus the P1-30B-A3B starting point; larger references: Gemini 3.1 Pro Thinking, GPT-5.5-High, DeepSeek-V3.2-Speciale.
Stage-wise progression on AnswerBench vs ProofBench across SFT / coarse RL / refined RL / TTS.
SFT data-ordering comparison (descending-PPL vs random vs ascending-PPL) on validation AnswerBench/AMO-Bench and truncation rate.
Token-length distribution of TTS actions (initial generation, refinement, verification, verdict) on USAMO 2026; cost comparison against DeepSeek-V3.2 and Nemotron-Cascade-2 training budgets.

key_findings.finding: With test-time scaling the 30B-A3B model attains gold-medal totals on official math olympiads, matching the top human score on USAMO 2026.
key_findings.evidence: Expert-graded 35/42 on both IMO 2025 (gold line 35) and USAMO 2026 (gold line 25), with 5 of 6 problems at full credit in each (IMO P6 and USAMO P2 unsolved); USAMO 2026 statistics report 340 competitors, median 6, and maximum 35. Direct generation without TTS gives 21 (IMO 2025) and 15 (USAMO 2026), above bronze lines.

key_findings.finding: The recipe yields the strongest similar-size proof-quality performance, with test-time verification/refinement adding a large further gain.
key_findings.evidence: IMO-ProofBench overall 57.6% direct (vs 52.9% Nemotron-Cascade-2, 23.1% Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, 20.0% for the P1-30B-A3B starting point) and 70.2% with TTS (91.0% basic, 49.5% advanced), close to Gemini 3.1 Pro Thinking's 72.6%.

key_findings.finding: Each pipeline stage plays a distinct, measurable role: SFT reshapes behavior at a temporary cost to answer accuracy, coarse RLVR restores and scales solving, and refined RL specifically improves hard proof problems.
key_findings.evidence: Stage trace: AnswerBench 69.2 → 59.8 after SFT → 77.2 after coarse RL → 77.5 final; ProofBench-Basic 33.8 → 57.6 → 76.7 → 77.1 → 91.0 (TTS); ProofBench-Advanced 6.2 → 14.8 → 25.2 → 38.1 → 49.5, i.e. refined RL's gain is concentrated on the advanced split.

key_findings.finding: Descending-perplexity (reverse) ordering of SFT data is critical for preserving backbone capability and avoiding degenerate long generations.
key_findings.evidence: Validation SFT runs: descending-PPL reaches 55.8 AnswerBench / 40.0 AMO-Bench with 0.3%/0.0% truncation, versus random ordering 39.5/31.0 with 7.3%/8.0% truncation, and ascending (low-PPL-first) ordering 24.3/15.0.

key_findings.finding: Specializing on math and physics signals transfers to untrained scientific domains and to research-level problems, and inference compute is spent mostly on very long generation and repair.
key_findings.evidence: FrontierScience-Olympiad 61.5% overall (69.4% chemistry, 25.0% biology) and best similar-size FrontierScience-Research score (11.7%) despite math/physics-only RL; IPhO 23.5/20.3 points direct (above the 20.8/19.7 gold lines) rising to 25.3/21.7 with TTS; TTS traces on USAMO 2026 show median lengths of 106K tokens for initial generation, 83K for refinement, 28.7K for verification, 404 for verdict.
